newsitem.title: UK: Tanker declared loss after Lagos blast - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Tanker declared loss after Lagos blast - Lloyds.

text.p: The chemical tanker Al Zainab which caught fire and exploded off Lagos on June 6 has been declared a constructive total loss and is likely to be sold for scrap, Lloyds Casualty said on Wednesday.
"The possibilities of her being repaired are extremely remote. It is most likely that she will be sold for scrap," Lloyds quoted London-based Britannic Maritime Ltd as saying.
A Britannic official declined to comment.

The 29,800 dwt vessel had an explosion and fire in its port wing tank while anchored at Commodore Pool, Apapa. Navy Captain Shuaibu Amodu, head of security at the port, said the explosion was caused by welding work.
At least two crew members were killed and hundreds of Lagos workers rushed from their offices in panic when they heard the explosion.
The St Vincent and Grenadines-flagged vessel is currently lying at a safe berth in Lagos, Lloyds said.
